items.title: open-docs
items.text:
A documentation generator for Terraform/OpenTofu modules, built on open-inspector.

The goal: a modern alternative to terraform-docs that matches its day-to-day workflow, then goes further using data the inspector captures that terraform-docs discards (source ranges, schema findings, reference graphs, structured types).

Early / proof-of-concept

Today open-docs emits a verbose, debug-oriented dump of everything the inspector parses. The curated, reader-facing output and several workflow features are planned; the feature checklist tracks what works now and what is coming.

items.title: Why open-docs
items.text:
terraform-docs renders the fields it understands and throws the rest away. open-inspector keeps the parts that make docs actionable, and open-docs turns them into output:

  • Source permalinks. Every block carries filename + start/end line:column:byte, so docs can deep-link to the exact source lines.
  • Health, not just a field dump. Schema findings (deprecated, unknown, missing-required attributes) and missing descriptions become an actionable checklist with severity.
  • Diagrams. The inspector's module graph becomes inline dependency and resource diagrams.
  • Richer data. Leading # ... doc-comments, structured variable types (object({ ... }) with optional), decoded default values, and expression-level references (var.x, module.y.z, aws_s3_bucket.b).
  • Fuller block coverage than terraform-docs: moved, import, removed, check, ephemeral, and OpenTofu encryption.

items.title: See it
items.text: The example gallery shows open-docs output for real modules, rendered exactly as the tool generates it.

items.title: How it works
items.text: open-docs calls inspector.Inspect(dir) to parse the module into a *model.Module, then walks that struct in internal/render to render Markdown tables. All HCL parsing lives in open-inspector; open-docs owns presentation only.

items.title: Configuration
items.text:
open-docs reads an optional .open-docs.hcl. Put it in the module directory or the repository root, or pass -config <file>. open-docs uses the nearest one, searching from the module directory up to the repository root.

Your file is decoded on top of the built-in defaults, so set only what you want to change.

items.title: main
items.text:
main {
  docsfile = "README.md" # relative to the module directory
  mode     = "inject"    # "stdout" (default) | "replace" | "inject"
  header   = false       # omit the module title line (default: true)
  verbose  = true        # add line:column:byte ranges to positions (default: false)
  version  = false       # omit the "generated with open-docs" line (default: true)
}
Mode Behavior stdout Print the docs. The default. replace Overwrite docsfile with the docs. inject Replace the text between <!-- BEGIN_OPEN_DOC --> and <!-- END_OPEN_DOC --> in docsfile, adding the region if it is missing.

The -m <mode> flag sets the mode from the command line, and -o <file> sets the output file. Both take precedence over the config file. -o alone is a shortcut for replace mode to that path; combine it with -m inject to update the markers in that file instead.

-show and -hide take comma-separated section block names, such as -hide locals,resources, and override each section's render switch for one run; -hide wins when both name a section. -check renders the docs and exits non-zero if writing them would change the docs file, without writing it.

items.title: Sections and columns
items.text:
Every section has a block with a render switch and one switch per column:

# Hide two columns of the inputs table.
variables {
  comment  = false
  position = false
}

# Drop the outputs section entirely.
outputs {
  render = false
}

items.title: Install
items.text:
Download a binary for Linux, macOS, or Windows from the latest release, or install with Go (the version in go.mod or newer):

go install github.com/remoterabbit/open-docs@latest

To build from source, clone the repository and run make build; the binary is written to bin/open-docs.

items.title: Generate docs
items.text:
Point open-docs at a module directory:

# print to stdout
open-docs ./examples/vpc

# write to a file (replace mode)
open-docs -o ./examples/vpc/README.md ./examples/vpc

# update the marked region of a file (inject mode)
open-docs -m inject -o ./examples/vpc/README.md ./examples/vpc

# skip sections for one run (block names from .open-docs.hcl)
open-docs -hide locals,resources ./examples/vpc

# in CI: fail if the README is out of date, without writing it
open-docs -check -o ./examples/vpc/README.md ./examples/vpc

items.title: Keep a README up to date
items.text:
Rather than overwriting a whole file, open-docs can update a region of a hand-written README. Add the markers where the generated docs should go:

# My Module

Hand-written intro.

<!-- BEGIN_OPEN_DOC -->
<!-- END_OPEN_DOC -->

Then set mode = "inject" in a .open-docs.hcl next to the module:

main {
  mode = "inject"
}

Running open-docs ./my-module now replaces only the text between the markers and leaves the rest of the file untouched. See Configuration for every option.

items.title: Add provider schema findings
items.text:
With -schema, open-docs asks tofu or terraform for the provider schemas and reports deprecated, unknown, and missing-required attributes:

open-docs -schema ./examples/vpc

Note

-schema needs tofu or terraform on your PATH and an initialized module (tofu init).

items.title: Example gallery
items.text:
Each page here is the README.md that open-docs generates for a module under examples/, shown as-is. Source links in the tables open the exact lines on GitHub.

  • vpc: a realistic multi-file AWS VPC module with a local child module.
  • complete: every block type open-inspector understands (including ephemeral, check, OpenTofu encryption and provider for_each, and a .tf.json file), plus table edge cases such as pipes, heredocs, Unicode, and long values.
  • invalid: deliberately broken configuration for the diagnostics table.

Defaults to the first three available in the region. - - - - 0 ./variables.tf public_subnets list(string) ["10.0.0.0/24", "10.0.1.0/24", "10.0.2.0/24"] CIDR blocks for public subnets, one per availability zone. - - - - 0 ./variables.tf private_subnets list(string) ["10.0.10.0/24", "10.0.11.0/24", "10.0.12.0/24"] CIDR blocks for private subnets, one per availability zone. - - - - 0 ./variables.tf database_subnets list(string) [] CIDR blocks for isolated database subnets. Leave empty to skip. - - - - 0 ./variables.tf enable_dns_hostnames bool true Enable DNS hostnames in the VPC. - - - - 0 ./variables.tf enable_dns_support bool true Enable DNS resolution in the VPC. - - - - 0 ./variables.tf enable_nat_gateway bool true Provision NAT gateways so private subnets can reach the internet. NAT gateways are the single largest cost in this module. In non-prod environments prefer single_nat_gateway = true. - - - 0 ./variables.tf single_nat_gateway bool false Share one NAT gateway across all private subnets instead of one per AZ. - - - - 0 ./variables.tf nat_gateway_config object({connectivity_type = optional(string, "public"), eip_allocation_ids = optional(list(string), []), reuse_eips = optional(bool, false), tags = optional(map(string), {})}) {} Advanced NAT gateway settings. - - - - 0 ./variables.tf flow_logs object({destination = optional(string, "cloud-watch-logs"), enabled = bool, replicate_to_dr = optional(bool, false), retention_in_days = optional(number, 30), traffic_type = optional(string, "ALL")}) {enabled = true} VPC flow log configuration. - - - - 2 ./variables.tf vpc_endpoints set(string) ["s3", "dynamodb"] Gateway or interface endpoint services to create, e.g. s3, ecr.api. - - - - 0 ./variables.tf import_existing_vpc_id string "" Adopt an existing VPC into state instead of creating a new one. - - - - 0 ./variables.tf vpn_preshared_key string null Pre-shared key for the optional site-to-site VPN connection. - ✓ - - 0 ./variables.tf tags map(string) {} Tags applied to all resources. - - ✗ - 0 ./variables.tf subnet_tags object({database = optional(map(string), {}), private = optional(map(string), {}), public = optional(map(string), {})}) {} Extra tags per subnet tier, merged over tags. - - ✗ - 0 ./variables.tf
